reason: This is the only available combination, and it connects the bodily rite to the competing accounts of creation.
expectation: I expect a comparison of what using physical objects for a spiritual gift might imply about bodies, though it may not settle who made them.

effect: The result clarified that a bodily rite does not establish who created matter, and that its appeal to Acts does not independently verify its promised gift.
reaction: The distinction between a ritual practice and a claim about creation was useful, though the chapter ended just as it became interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the bodily rite to the competing creation accounts was worthwhile because it showed the limits of what the rite itself can establish.

leastWorthwhile.text: The chapter offered only one combination, so there was little opportunity to make a meaningful choice.

surprise.text: The result distinguished renouncing worldly desires from abandoning other people, citing the pledge to pray for persecutors.

arbitrary.text: The combination had a clear purpose, although the menu made it the only available action.

continue.text: I would continue to see these distinctions tested in a chapter with more meaningful choices; this one made me curious but was very brief.
